Thank you, and what this page is

Thank you for your email of Wednesday 28 October and for the two documents: ASSET Voyages website redesign requirements (version 0.4, 28 October 2026) and the one-page Developer initial proposal form.

This page is our first reply. It sets out what we understood, what the new site would need to run, and the questions we need answered. We send the full priced proposal within 24–48 working hours of receiving your answers.

What is included. The concept, the console and the assumptions on this page are illustrations to help you answer; they are not a list of what is included. What is included is set only by the signed proposal. The proposal, once signed, is our contract.

More qualified enquiries. The site should bring in real requests for business travel, for events, and for congress flights, not just visits.

Small-business owner or office manager: reads the offer for small firms, then asks for an account or a demo.
Travel manager: sees your approach and evidence, then requests a review of their travel.
HR or communications manager: explores event services, then sends a step-by-step brief and gets a call back.
Congress participant: finds the congress, opens its page, and requests a flight quote that ASSET prepares.
Existing client: clicks “Client login” and goes straight to the client tool. No password is kept on the website.
A website built for you and owned by you, with its own admin, the “ASSET Console”.

Our recommendation: a custom build. Your current site runs on WordPress, a sound and widely used choice. For the new portal we recommend a site built for you, with its own admin and no paid plugins to keep updated. The audit of your current site (step J1) will confirm whether to keep or replace it, with the costs of each option. If the audit changes the approach, the change is agreed in writing with its effect on price and dates.
Ms Khatri publishes directly. The Console lets her edit pages, add or import congresses from a spreadsheet, and follow every enquiry, without a developer.

Everything in ASSET’s name. The domain, the hosting and every account belong to ASSET. At handover you receive the full source, and once the delivered work is paid you can move to another supplier under the exit terms in the signed proposal.
Security of your congress codes. The private event codes from Air France–KLM (GM&E codes) stay in the locked admin area and never reach the public site. Fewer moving parts means less to keep secure.
Speed on phones. The public pages are prepared in advance and served from close to the visitor, so they open quickly even on a weak mobile connection.
Ownership. Nothing is rented from us; maintenance is an optional monthly plan. If you change supplier, your site, code, data and accounts go with you, under the exit terms.
Low running cost. About €5–15 a month in provider fees (see section 4).

The alternative. A ready-made content editor such as Directus, installed on a rented server. It is a sound product and would meet the brief. It does mean a server to rent, update and watch, so more hosting cost and more upkeep each month.
Issuing tickets, and the flight booking engine. The website collects the request; your team prepares the quote and issues tickets in your usual tools.
Also outside: paid CRM software, bulk scraping, automatic publication, photography, and copywriting beyond question 9. The full list comes with the proposal.

Preparing your new website: what we understood, what it needs, and what we need from you.
Our understanding of your request for proposal, the running costs to expect, a few observations, and our 30 questions.
ASSET Voyages management, and Ms Veena Khatri (coordination)
Thank you, and what this page is

Thank you for your email of Wednesday 28 October and for the two documents: ASSET Voyages website redesign requirements (version 0.4, 28 October 2026) and the one-page Developer initial proposal form.

This page is our first reply. It sets out what we understood, what the new site would need to run, and the questions we need answered. We send the full priced proposal within 24–48 working hours of receiving your answers.

What is included. The concept, the console and the assumptions on this page are illustrations to help you answer; they are not a list of what is included. What is included is set only by the signed proposal. The proposal, once signed, is our contract.
There are three companion pages. Like this one, they are unlisted: hidden from Google and not linked from any public site, but anyone with the link can open them.
A first visual direction, with a working demo of the congress search. Sample data only.
Today’s site compared with the concept (in French).
A preview of the proposed admin for publishing pages and congresses and following enquiries.
Your brief lists four expected outcomes. In our words:
More qualified enquiries. The site should bring in real requests for business travel, for events, and for congress flights, not just visits.
Publishing without a developer. Ms Khatri and a backup editor should be able to update pages and add congresses themselves.

Keep the value Google already gives you. Today’s addresses found in our scan and in Search Console are mapped and redirected to their closest new page, and today’s site stays live until the new one is approved. (No supplier can guarantee rankings.)
Ready for later, not dependent on it. Links with Wondermiles or Air France–KLM can come later. The launch must not wait for them.
Business travel for companies, from small firms to travel and purchasing managers.
Events (MICE): meetings, incentive trips, conferences and exhibitions, including seminars and group travel.
International congresses: helping participants find a congress and request flights to it.
Who visits, and what they should be able to do
Small-business owner or office manager: reads the offer for small firms, then asks for an account or a demo.
Travel manager: sees your approach and evidence, then requests a review of their travel.
HR or communications manager: explores event services, then sends a step-by-step brief and gets a call back.
Congress participant: finds the congress, opens its page, and requests a flight quote that ASSET prepares.
Existing client: clicks “Client login” and goes straight to the client tool. No password is kept on the website.
A website built for you and owned by you, with its own admin, the “ASSET Console”.

Our recommendation: a custom build. Your current site runs on WordPress, a sound and widely used choice. For the new portal we recommend a site built for you, with its own admin and no paid plugins to keep updated. The audit of your current site (step J1) will confirm whether to keep or replace it, with the costs of each option. If the audit changes the approach, the change is agreed in writing with its effect on price and dates.
Ms Khatri publishes directly. The Console lets her edit pages, add or import congresses from a spreadsheet, and follow every enquiry, without a developer.

Everything in ASSET’s name. The domain, the hosting and every account belong to ASSET. At handover you receive the full source, and once the delivered work is paid you can move to another supplier under the exit terms in the signed proposal.
Security of your congress codes. The private event codes from Air France–KLM (GM&E codes) stay in the locked admin area and never reach the public site. Fewer moving parts means less to keep secure.
Speed on phones. The public pages are prepared in advance and served from close to the visitor, so they open quickly even on a weak mobile connection.
Ownership. Nothing is rented from us; maintenance is an optional monthly plan. If you change supplier, your site, code, data and accounts go with you, under the exit terms.
Low running cost. About €5–15 a month in provider fees (see section 4).

The alternative. A ready-made content editor such as Directus, installed on a rented server. It is a sound product and would meet the brief. It does mean a server to rent, update and watch, so more hosting cost and more upkeep each month.
Issuing tickets, and the flight booking engine. The website collects the request; your team prepares the quote and issues tickets in your usual tools.
Also outside: paid CRM software, bulk scraping, automatic publication, photography, and copywriting beyond question 9. The full list comes with the proposal.
None of these is needed for launch. Each would be priced separately in the proposal.
English version, especially for congress pages.
Connection to a customer-relationship tool, so each enquiry lands in your sales system automatically.
Wondermiles link-up: for example, one login for clients across the site and the tool, if Wondermiles allows it.
AI helper that finds new congresses for your team to check. Nothing is published without a person approving it.
What runs behind the scenes, and what it costs you

The new site relies on a small set of hosted services. For each one: what it does, who provides it, and what ASSET would pay that provider each month. These amounts are paid to the providers directly, not to us.
Hosts the site and delivers it quickly anywhere in the world
Runs the admin, the forms and the enquiry list

Two-step login for staff, only for named work email addresses: either your work email account (Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, with its own two-step check switched on), or a one-time code sent to the work email plus an authenticator app or security key (question 26)
Daily backups kept 30 days: the database can be restored to any minute of the last 30 days; photos and documents to the previous day
An outside check every 5 minutes that the site is up, with email alerts
Page-visit statistics that use no cookies, so they add nothing to your cookie banner
Counts button clicks, form starts and sends, errors, congress searches and page views, account requests and client-login clicks, with no cookies and no personal data
A separate test copy of the site, open only to your team, where changes are checked first

A few observations from reading your brief and your current site. Most are quick decisions.
Client login. Your current client area says “Connexion Traveldoo”, while the brief mentions Wondermiles. Is Wondermiles replacing Traveldoo? (Question 23.)

Two domain names. Your site runs on asset-voyagesdaffaires.com; the brief’s letterhead shows assetvoyages.com. We suggest choosing one as the main address and redirecting the other to it, so Google sees one site.
Copyright year. The current footer shows both “©2020” and “© 2026”. Worth aligning before launch.
“Plus de 122 agences”. The Selectour Affaires figure on your site is undated. Your brief asks for claims to be checked before reuse, so we would re-confirm it.
The congress catalogue is the biggest new value. It does not exist today. A searchable list, one page per congress, and a flight quote request already filled in with the congress details.
Past congresses need a rule. Keep them as an archive, or remove them. Either is fine; we need your choice. (Question 21.)
Statistics without cookies. Visitor statistics can work without cookies, which keeps the site lighter and the banner shorter.

We follow the seven milestones in your brief. Each one ends with a deliverable and your written approval. Dates go in the proposal: work starts within 5 working days of the signed proposal, and launch follows about 12 weeks after the start (question 1).

Monitoring, fixes of defects against the accepted tests, handover of code, access and exports. After these 4 weeks, support and fixes are covered by the optional maintenance plan or quoted per request.
Rounds of changes: two per design stage and two per content stage (page wording included, see question 9). Further rounds are quoted first.
Nothing goes live without written approval from ASSET management. No change to your current site or domain happens before that.

Please return your answers as one PDF to debanjan@prodcraft.fyi by Friday 6 November. Fill in the PDF directly, or use the Word version and save it as PDF. 1Answer first When is the proposal due, and when do you plan to choose a supplier? Is there a date the new site has to be live by, or a busy period when it should not launch?

If we don’t hear back, we’ll assume: we send the proposal within 24–48 working hours of receiving your answers, or by 10 November if no answers arrive by 6 November; work starts within 5 working days of the signed proposal; launch about 12 weeks after the start, moving day for day with any late input; no launch between 21 December and 1 January.
2Answer first Is there a budget range or a cap for the core site and the Congress catalogue? A rough bracket is enough.

3Answer first Who at ASSET approves each stage (design, content, launch), and does each activity (Business Travel, MICE, Congresses) sign off its own pages? How many working days should we plan for each approval?

If we don’t hear back, we’ll assume: ASSET management approves each stage in writing (directly, or through Ms Khatri on its behalf) within 3 working days, in one combined reply for all three activities. 14Which journeys should be in English first, from when (launch or later), and who will translate?

16Which sales tools do you use today: a CRM, a newsletter or email-marketing tool, or email only?

26Does your team sign in with Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace? We’d use it for a secure two-step login to the admin area.

Our understanding of your request for proposal, the running costs to expect, a few observations, and our 30 questions.

Thank you, and what this page is

Thank you for your email of Wednesday 28 October and for the two documents: ASSET Voyages website redesign requirements (version 0.4, 28 October 2026) and the one-page Developer initial proposal form.

This page is our first reply. It sets out what we understood, what the new site would need to run, and the questions we need answered. We send the full priced proposal within 24–48 working hours of receiving your answers.

What is included. The concept, the console and the assumptions on this page are illustrations to help you answer; they are not a list of what is included. What is included is set only by the signed proposal. The proposal, once signed, is our contract.

More qualified enquiries. The site should bring in real requests for business travel, for events, and for congress flights, not just visits.

Everything in ASSET’s name. The domain, the hosting and every account belong to ASSET. At handover you receive the full source, and once the delivered work is paid you can move to another supplier under the exit terms in the signed proposal.

Speed on phones. The public pages are prepared in advance and served from close to the visitor, so they open quickly even on a weak mobile connection.
Ownership. Nothing is rented from us; maintenance is an optional monthly plan. If you change supplier, your site, code, data and accounts go with you, under the exit terms.
Low running cost. About €5–15 a month in provider fees (see section 4).

The alternative. A ready-made content editor such as Directus, installed on a rented server. It is a sound product and would meet the brief. It does mean a server to rent, update and watch, so more hosting cost and more upkeep each month.
Issuing tickets, and the flight booking engine. The website collects the request; your team prepares the quote and issues tickets in your usual tools.
Also outside: paid CRM software, bulk scraping, automatic publication, photography, and copywriting beyond question 9. The full list comes with the proposal.
None of these is needed for launch. Each would be priced separately in the proposal.
English version, especially for congress pages.

Congress filters built from your sample list, and one page per edition of a congress.
